principles: No assumed sync: every alignment claim needs a file or command reference.
No self-judging: Claude performs audit execution, Codex verifies high-risk claims independently.
No production code changes in this audit story.
Follow-up implementation must be split by repository ownership.
drivers: User asked to follow Koala flow and make Claude Code execute.
B-ca8f made Koala CLI converge, but cross-end behavior still needs explicit verification.
INIT reviewer advisory requires CHK-002 to be broken into per-surface DoneWhen.

options.name: audit-only cross-end verification
pros: Low risk and matches the current unknowns.
Keeps follow-up work assigned to the correct repository.
cons: Does not itself fix any discovered gap.
Requires a second implementation story if blockers are found.

options.name: immediate cross-repo implementation
pros: Could fix gaps in one pass if already known.
May feel faster when confidence is high.
cons: Discovery and implementation would be mixed across three repositories.
Higher chance of modifying the wrong contract surface or bypassing each repo Koala flow.

options.name: Koala CLI-only validation
cons: Does not answer whether Cord Team authority and Mac/Swift surfaces are aligned.
Would leave the core user concern unresolved.

rationale: Choose audit-only first because the current risk is unknown cross-end alignment, not a known code defect. The audit can produce exact follow-up stories after evidence is collected.

preMortem.scenario: The audit becomes a vague narrative.
preMortem.trigger: Claude writes conclusions without per-surface rows or file references.
preMortem.consequence: Codex cannot verify the report and follow-up stories may be wrong.
preMortem.mitigation: Require a contract matrix with file references and verification evidence for every high-risk claim.

preMortem.scenario: The audit reports green by assumption.
preMortem.trigger: Command outcomes or contract fields are summarized without raw output.
preMortem.consequence: The story recreates the fact-forgery risk it is supposed to reduce.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep CHK-001 neutral and record pass/fail raw command outputs exactly.

preMortem.trigger: Existing active backlog is not checked before recommendations.
preMortem.consequence: Work fragments across multiple stories and future agents get conflicting ownership.
preMortem.mitigation: Compare recommendations against B-4622, B-da5b, and relevant cross-end backlog before marking CHK-003 done.
